evidence: Plaut. Men. 2.3.86: jamne ībis?, are you going so soon? (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 52: obsolēvit jam ista ōrātiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Jamne …? asks “already?”. With a negative, “no longer”: jam nōn, nōn jam; “not yet” is nōndum (see not yet).

terms.gloss: for a long time already (with a present tense)
evidence: Ter. Eun. 816: Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.
Cic. Fam. 7.9.1: jam diū ignōrō quid agās
Traupman 88: I’ve been here a long time already, jam dūdum adsum
terms.comment: Latin keeps the present where English says “have been”: jam dūdum adsum, I’ve been here for ages (Traupman 88).

phrases.latin: Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.
phrases.english: My mind’s been on the dishes for ages.

phrases.latin: jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis
phrases.english: I haven’t known how you are for a long time now; you don’t write
